language_scope: en only (G1 English-first evaluation sequence); the case shape carries a language tag so later MSA, Kuwaiti / Gulf and Egyptian packs use the same contract
purpose: Pre-creation interpretation of an ordinary-language idea for the existing /start integrated-invention choice; no project, account or real inventor data
matching_rule: Reference substrings, terms and stems are matched case-insensitively against the registry-normalised, whitespace-collapsed reply text.
input_rule: Only idea_text is ever sent to a separately authorised provider run; case_id, language, labels and reference annotations are never sent.

cases.idea_text: I want to develop a small electronic device with a circuit board inside an enclosure, but I have not decided the components or dimensions.
I want to develop a small electronic device built on a single circuit board that plugs straight into a laptop. I have not chosen the components yet.
I want a small electronic gadget on a circuit board. It might end up in some kind of box, or it might not; I have not thought about that yet.
I want a desk lamp that tilts its arm toward me by itself: a small motor moves the arm and a light sensor on a control board tells it when to move.
I want a wooden stand that holds a tablet at a comfortable reading angle.
Inspired by the way Arduino hobbyists organize their kits, I want a folding cardboard organizer for screws and small tools.
I want a bare circuit board that monitors room temperature. I do not want any case, housing or cover around it.
I want something that makes my mornings less stressful.
I want a little gadget that beeps when my houseplant needs water. I have no idea what should go inside it.
I need a weatherproof housing for a sensor board I already have. I don't know the board's size yet or how it should be mounted.
I'd like to tuck the little green electronics card from my hobby project into a shell that snaps together.
Picture a PCB living inside a 3D-printed casing that clips onto a bike handlebar.
A table lamp whose wiring and switch are hidden inside a hand-carved wooden base.
For now it is only a circuit board that blinks a light. If I ever add a case later, that would be a separate idea.
My neighbour's doorbell sits in a plastic case. I only want to design a new circuit that makes it play a tune.
A hand-cranked coffee grinder with nothing electric in it at all.
A cabinet door that unlocks itself when someone types the right code on a battery-powered keypad.
A phone app that reminds me to drink water every hour.
An electronic kitchen timer on one circuit board, which I will sell packed in a cardboard box.
A plant pot that tips water into the soil on a timer; no pump, just a small electric valve and a timer circuit.
